findings.title: Four Requests to Root: A Cacti 0day (4http2shell PoC)
findings.summary_md: Researcher ek0ms savi0r, publishing under Church of Malware, uploaded the original writeup and proof-of-concept code for 4HTTP2SHELL (also called 4HTTP2ROOT). The chain moves from a fresh anonymous session to a shell in four requests: a guest write of `preview_graphs_per_page`, a stacked `UPDATE` of `poller_item.arg1` through the `graph_view.php` preview LIMIT clause, then `graph_realtime.php?action=init` reaching `popen()`. It was demonstrated against Cacti 1.2.31 in a lab where the web tier ran as root.

findings.title: Cacti Zero-Day: What We Know So Far
findings.summary_md: Previdian Research reports lab verification of the guest-to-command chain against Cacti 1.2.31, described as insufficient validation of a guest-writable setting producing a stored second-order SQL injection. The post states no official patch had been identified and Cacti's advisories and the 1.2.31 release notes do not name the `preview_graphs_per_page` setting. It tracks the issue as VULN-2026-0010 and names disabling the guest user as the interim mitigation.

findings.title: GHSA-gp82-qhrg-crv7: Pre-Authentication SQL Injection via unanchored FILTER_VALIDATE_REGEXP in graph_view.php
findings.summary_md: Cacti published a pre-authentication SQL injection advisory for `graph_view.php` affecting versions up to and including 1.2.30, fixed by the 1.2.31 release. The flaw was reachable without credentials on installs that had guest graph viewing enabled, the same precondition the current zero-day requires.

findings.title: GHSA-69gg-mjfm-jjpc: Pre-authentication SQL injection via rfilter RLIKE clause in graph_view.php
findings.summary_md: CVE-2026-39893 covers the `rfilter` variable being concatenated into a SQL `RLIKE` clause in `graph_view.php`, reachable pre-auth where guest viewing was enabled. Cacti fixed it in 1.2.31 through PR #7054, adding `db_qstr_rlike()` to cap length and strip metacharacters before quoting. It documents a second pre-authentication injection in the same file months before the zero-day.

findings.title: Cacti v1.2.31 release
findings.summary_md: Cacti v1.2.31 was published on 15 June 2026 and is the release the public exploit targets. It remains the newest stable tag, which is why the PoC against 1.2.31 applies to current installations rather than only to old ones.
